topics.title: Install and update
topics.prerequisites: Requires a supported OS/architecture and network for downloads; source builds require the pinned Rust toolchain. Installation writes the chosen binary directory; Windows may update user PATH.

sections.title: install
sections.body:
Linux/macOS: `curl -fsSL https://github.com/pixelinfinito/rio/releases/latest/download/install.sh -o install.sh`; inspect, then `sh install.sh`. Windows: download the same release's `install.ps1`, inspect it, then run `.\install.ps1`. Published releases, not this source checkout, determine what latest installs; stable acceptance remains pending in the repository records.
`rio --version` prints version, target and commit. Unix default: `~/.local/bin`; Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\rio\bin`. Add the Unix directory to PATH yourself. Windows `-NoModifyPath` avoids changing PATH.

sections.title: versions
sections.body:
`sh install.sh --version VERSION --install-dir DIR`; Windows `-Version VERSION -InstallDir DIR`. Substitute an existing tag for VERSION. Flags override `RIO_VERSION`/`RIO_INSTALL_DIR`. Installers verify SHA-256 before replacement. `gh attestation verify ARCHIVE --repo pixelinfinito/rio` verifies provenance. `RIO_DOWNLOAD_BASE` accepts HTTPS or a local archive/checksum directory.
Source: install Rust from `rust-toolchain.toml`, then `cargo install --path crates/rio-cli --locked`. `RIO_BUILD_VERSION`/`RIO_BUILD_COMMIT` identify archive builds.

sections.title: remove
sections.body: Rerun installer to upgrade/downgrade. `sh install.sh --uninstall` or `.\install.ps1 -Uninstall` keeps personal config; add `--purge`/`-Purge` to delete it. Environment equivalents: `RIO_UNINSTALL=1`, `RIO_PURGE=1`. Source install: `cargo uninstall rio-cli`. Repository caches require deliberate separate removal. Unsupported platforms/checksum failures install nothing; keep the old binary and correct target/download source.

topics.title: Review changes
topics.prerequisites: Requires a Git working tree, project dependencies and installed toolchains. Review executes project tools/tests and writes snapshots/reports to the cache. Hosted mode sends selected source to the configured endpoint; use --offline to keep Rio local.

sections.title: selection
sections.body:
`rio review --format json` reviews tracked/staged changes and untracked nonignored files against HEAD. `--staged` selects only the index. `--base origin/main` selects committed HEAD against the merge base, not local edits. Selection flags conflict. `--profile NAME_OR_PATH` chooses a profile. No endpoint: deterministic checks/graph run; agents/verifiers are deferred (`no_endpoint`).
`--offline` prevents Rio network calls, not network from tools/tests. Install dependencies yourself; Rio does not install them. To avoid terminal UI use `--no-tui`, `RIO_TUI=0`, or an explicit `--format terminal|json|md|sarif`. `--no-color`, `NO_COLOR`, and redirects disable color; `--ascii`/`RIO_ASCII=1` use ASCII glyphs.

sections.title: hosted
sections.body:
Configured endpoint and online mode required for `--pr NUMBER`, `--preset quick|standard|deep`, `--deep`, `--publish`, `--since-last`, `--fork`. `--deep` conflicts with `--preset`. `--nightly` marks a nightly evaluation run for council triggers. `--fork` marks the local submission; PR mode derives fork status at the endpoint.
`rio review --since-last` continues branch lineage; `--reset-lineage` requires it and starts a new generation. Detached HEAD is invalid for lineage. See github for PR publishing and feedback for rounds.

sections.title: interpret
sections.body: `--show-pre-existing` reveals baseline findings; `--show-remembered` lists remembered dismissals without changing policy. Exit 0: no policy failure, possibly skipped optional checks; 1: policy finding; 2: usage/config; 3: repository/internal; 4: incomplete/required-check failure; 5: PR publication failure after a passing review; 130: second interrupt. Inspect check statuses even on 0. First Ctrl-C preserves partial results; second stops processes and emits no JSON document. SIGTERM counts as an interrupt; with an endpoint, the second interrupt waits up to 30 s for the endpoint to accept cancellation.

topics.title: Diagnose readiness
topics.prerequisites: Run in the project with its dependencies installed. Doctor probes tools and checks cache readiness; with an endpoint it also checks protocol/GitHub setup. --rotate changes the GitHub App webhook secret.

sections.title: commands
sections.body: `rio doctor --format json` explains effective settings and their sources, repository/HEAD, profile validity, cache/free space, tools, dependency compatibility, and the same review plan used by review. `--staged` or `--base REF` selects the comparison. `--all-roots` inspects every detected project, including roots outside the diff; clean diffs otherwise schedule no root probes.

sections.title: recovery
sections.body:
Missing tool: install the project's pinned dependency/toolchain, then rerun. `dependency_mismatch`: synchronize installed dependencies to the selected lockfile. `trust_installed_dependencies: true` in rio/checks permits unknown compatibility, never a known mismatch. Baseline-unavailable findings outside changed hunks plus three lines of context are treated as pre-existing.
Cache error: check path/permissions/free space in effective settings. Invalid profile: `rio profile validate`. GitHub warning: install the app on the origin repository and check endpoint credentials. `rio doctor --rotate` rotates the webhook secret with rollback handling; use only when rotation is intended.

sections.title: exits
sections.body: 0 means no blocking configuration/profile/repository/cache problem; missing tools and skipped checks are warnings. 1 means a blocking readiness problem. These codes differ from review's finding/incomplete codes. Malformed arguments exit 2. Diagnostics must not be interpreted as a complete review.

topics.title: Read review results
topics.prerequisites: Read the report's status, checks and evidence, not only its finding count. Report/cache files can contain source; handle them like repository data.

sections.title: evidence
sections.body: Findings have category, severity, evidence_level, state, location and identity. Categories distinguish defects/security/risks; evidence distinguishes plausible from static_proven/reproduced. Pre-existing findings differ from new/worsened. Default fail_on targets new/worsened defects at static_proven or stronger, not every suggestion. A failed check, a skipped tool and a passing check are different outcomes. Zero findings with incomplete checks is not a clean result.

sections.title: output
sections.body:
`rio review --format json > report.json` emits one rio-report-v1 document; progress goes to stderr. Status: complete, incomplete, partial, no_changes, error. After parsing, config/repository errors also emit JSON; parser errors and second interrupt do not. `--format md > report.md` produces Markdown; exits 2/3 emit no Markdown document. `--format sarif > rio.sarif` emits SARIF 2.1.0, including invocation errors on exits 2/3. `--format terminal` streams without TUI.
Review ID identifies snapshot/profile inputs; run ID identifies an execution. Artifacts live under `<cache>/<review-id>/runs/<run-id>/`; latest identifies the most recently finished run.

sections.title: policy
sections.body: 0 no policy failure (optional skips possible); 1 matching finding; 2 usage/configuration; 3 repository/internal/persistence error; 4 incomplete/cancelled/required check per policy; 130 second interrupt. PR publication can add exit 5 after an otherwise passing review. A failing finding takes precedence over incomplete exit 4. `fail_on.incomplete: false` changes incomplete handling; `fail_on.required_checks: [typecheck, lint]` makes missing required checks fail. Doctor and QA sync have separate meanings.

topics.title: Terminal interface
topics.prerequisites: Review, QA and setup open the TUI when stdin/stdout are terminals, no explicit --format is given and CI is unset. Minimum size 80x24. UI strings remain English. --no-tui or RIO_TUI=0 selects streaming output.

sections.title: navigation
sections.body:
`?` help/view map; `:` command palette; Tab next pane; arrows or j/k move; Enter open; Esc back; `/` search; q quit (offers to save unsaved report). Review begins with source/profile/preset selection, then live progress and findings. Open a finding for hunk/evidence; export from the summary. Use the current help for context-specific keys.
`F` finding history, `S` suppression proposals, `P` PR publish preview. A security finding can open trace/council detail. Publishing and applying profile changes require explicit confirmation in the UI. A palette entry does not imply every action is available in every mode.

sections.title: qa
sections.body: Journey selection leads to a live viewport/scheme matrix; Enter opens cell details/evidence. Local matrix `p` pauses new cells (budget clock continues); `c` cancels the focused cell. Hosted queues do not support these controls. In completed cell detail `r` reruns that cell, but exported report and exit code retain the original run. Below 120 columns, `v` switches detail/screenshot view.

sections.title: recovery
sections.body: First Ctrl-C cancels tools and preserves partial report; second kills remaining tools and exits 130. SIGTERM closes the UI like quitting, stopping a running review first. `--ascii`/RIO_ASCII=1 addresses double-width box drawing; NO_COLOR removes color without removing state labels. Enlarge the terminal or use --no-tui if too small. Setup failures record a resumable step; retry in the UI or later with `rio deploy`.

topics.title: Profiles and policy
topics.prerequisites: Profiles define repository review behavior. Edit .rio/profiles/default.yaml deliberately and commit changes with the code; machine credentials/configuration belong in the user directory. Validate before review.

sections.title: selection
sections.body:
`rio profile list` shows built-in, personal and repository profiles and marks the default. `rio profile show rio/base` prints resolved YAML; `rio profile show strict --raw` prints authored YAML. `rio profile validate [NAME_OR_PATH]` exits 0 if valid, 2 if invalid, reporting YAML paths.
Default precedence: repository .rio/profiles/default.yaml, personal profiles/default.yaml, rio/base. Named profiles and explicit paths work with `rio review --profile strict`. Built-ins include base, openrouter, anthropic, security, critical and qa; list the installed binary for the exact set.

sections.title: inheritance
sections.body: Use `version: 1`, a name and `extends: rio/base`. Maps merge; lists replace. Overriding steps requires listing every step you want to keep, including prepare and report and valid needs dependencies. `rio profile show NAME` checks the resolved result. Unknown modules, invalid options or dependency cycles stop validation before tools run.

sections.title: recipes
sections.body:
To require tools, extend rio/base and set `fail_on: {required_checks: [typecheck, lint]}`. To keep incomplete analysis from exit 4, set `fail_on: {incomplete: false}`; reports still show incompleteness. For coverage off, copy the resolved steps and set `coverage: false` under the rio/checks step's with block. Exclusions go in rio/prepare `with.exclude`; suppressions go in top-level suppress, with documented reasons. Suppression proposals provide validated entries; see suppressions.
Other controls: max_lines (default 1500), posture balanced, rounds cap 3/diff_only_after 1, publish never|ask|auto, always_human, security, council, models, budget and rules. Inspect schemas/module docs for exact keys using `rio docs modules` and `rio docs budgets`. Local agents/verification defer without an endpoint.

topics.title: Machine configuration
topics.prerequisites: Machine configuration is user-owned; Rio never reads these settings from a cloned repository. Invalid keys/values are errors even when another source overrides them. Do not store secrets in repository profiles.

sections.title: paths
sections.body: Config directory: RIO_CONFIG_DIR; else XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rio; else ~/.config/rio (Linux/macOS), or APPDATA/rio on Windows with USERPROFILE/.config/rio fallback. File: config.toml; personal profiles: profiles/. Flags override matching environment values, then file, then defaults. `rio doctor --format json` shows effective values/sources.

sections.title: settings
sections.body:
endpoint.url / RIO_ENDPOINT_URL: unset by default. cache.dir / RIO_CACHE_DIR: repository .rio/cache. cache.max_age / RIO_CACHE_MAX_AGE: 30d. cache.max_size / RIO_CACHE_MAX_SIZE: 5GiB. cache.retain_raw_output / RIO_CACHE_RETAIN_RAW_OUTPUT: true. run.parallelism / RIO_PARALLELISM: physical cores capped at 4. run.output_limit / RIO_OUTPUT_LIMIT: 256MiB per tool stream.
Example config.toml: `[cache]` with `max_age = "7d"`, `max_size = "2GiB"`, `retain_raw_output = false`; `[run]` with `parallelism = 2`, `output_limit = "128MiB"`. Positive parallelism required. Sizes accept byte counts or units; ages accept durations/days.

sections.title: credentials
sections.body: Endpoint API token: RIO_API_TOKEN or configured credential store; connect with `rio init --endpoint URL --token-stdin` using secret-manager stdin. Deployment choices are under [deployment], GitHub App identifiers under [github_app]. `rio deploy --dry-run` inspects deployment without mutation. Provider keys use environment/private secrets files or keychain, not arguments. `NO_COLOR`, RIO_ASCII and RIO_TUI control terminal display; see tui. For a bad config, correct the named file/key and rerun doctor.

topics.title: Deploy or connect
topics.prerequisites: Deploying creates or updates resources in your Cloudflare account and may incur costs. Requires cf authentication or CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, eligible account services and model credentials. Sandbox image transfer also needs Docker; self-hosted deployment does not need Docker on the deploying machine.

sections.title: connect
sections.body: Existing endpoint: `rio init --endpoint https://YOUR-ENDPOINT --token-stdin`, providing API token on stdin. This saves user pairing configuration. `rio doctor` checks compatibility. API keys never belong in URLs or arguments. Endpoint connection conflicts with deployment flags.

sections.title: deploy
sections.body:
`cf auth login`, then `rio init` opens setup. Supply OPENROUTER_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY privately. `rio init --no-tui` uses terminal prompts. For scripted setup: --account ID, --name NAME, --cf-profile PROFILE, --runner sandbox|self-hosted, --runner-image IMAGE, --workers-subdomain NAME, --credential-store keychain|file, --secrets-file PRIVATE_JSON. --default-model and --verifier-model choose routes. --from CONFIG replays saved choices. --dry-run prints a plan without account changes.
Rio embeds the paired Worker; no npm/Wrangler checkout build is needed. It provisions Worker, Workflows, D1, R2, queue, AI Gateway and optional Sandbox in your account. Config stores choices; credentials use keychain by default or private files when explicitly selected. On headless machines choose file only if desired.

sections.title: maintain
sections.body:
`rio deploy` upgrades/reuses saved resources and resumes partial deployment. Rotate provider credentials privately and redeploy. Deployments never silently take over another Worker's bindings. `rio init --github-app [--github-org ORG]` adds PR integration. `rio init --replace-private-key FILE.pem` updates the registered App key. --council-vendor entries and --no-council manage council opt-in; see council.
For self-hosted execution configure the paired rio-runner/Docker host to poll the endpoint with its separate runner secret. Keep app source execution isolated from control-plane credentials. Authentication errors: verify cf profile/account and services; endpoint protocol errors: upgrade paired CLI/Worker/runner together.

sections.title: self-hosted
sections.body: On a dedicated trusted Linux Docker host, check out matching Rio source. Privately supply RIO_RUNNER_SECRET=endpoint RUNNER_SECRET. Run `docker build -f worker/Dockerfile -t rio-runner:local .`, then `RIO_ENDPOINT_URL=https://YOUR-ENDPOINT cargo run --locked -p rio-runner -- serve --image rio-runner:local`. The local tag is a checkout-built image, not a release number. Keep polling active with a service manager. Never mount Docker socket, host workspace or credentials inside analysis containers.

topics.title: Model providers
topics.prerequisites: AI review needs an online configured endpoint, model routes in the chosen profile and provider credentials. Provider calls may send selected source/evidence outside the account and consume money. Secrets must use environment/keychain/private files.

sections.title: standard
sections.body: `rio review --profile rio/openrouter --preset standard` selects the built-in OpenRouter profile after setup. `rio profile show rio/openrouter` reveals actual model aliases/routes. Anthropic has a built-in profile too. rio/base has no model routes; choosing it does not configure AI by itself. Gateway authentication and provider credentials are separate.

sections.title: custom
sections.body:
During init use `--custom-provider SLUG:PROTOCOL:BASE_URL`, where PROTOCOL is openai or anthropic. Supply `AI_GATEWAY_PROVIDER_KEY_<SLUG>` (normalized environment suffix) privately; inspect setup's instructions for the slug. Profiles reference custom-SLUG/MODEL. AI Gateway's unified compat/ routes and dynamic/ROUTE are supported when registered/configured. Never embed credentials in BASE_URL.
Deployment configuration stores custom provider metadata, optional model prices and dynamic routes, not provider keys. Provider/model routing errors must be fixed in deployment/profile configuration, then validated and redeployed as needed. A route marked unavailable must not be treated as successful verification.

sections.title: caching
sections.body: Provider prompt caching differs from gateway response caching. Deployment [deployment.prompt] cache/layout switches control supported prompt-cache hints and stable prompt layout. AI Gateway response caching and prompt logging are disabled by deployment. Read usage provenance in the report: cache read/write tokens can differ from normal input tokens. See budgets for ceilings; cached hypotheses still receive verification.

topics.title: Depth and spending
topics.prerequisites: Hosted presets require an endpoint and model configuration. More agents/voters consume more resources. Limits belong in the selected profile; exact defaults are version-specific and visible with rio profile show.

sections.title: presets
sections.body: `rio review --preset quick|standard|deep`; `--deep` is the deep shorthand and conflicts with --preset. Quick narrows agent/verification work; standard is the everyday option; deep spends more on high-risk analysis. A preset does not install dependencies or configure credentials. Start with standard on a small diff, inspect usage and incomplete steps before increasing depth.

sections.title: profile
sections.body:
budget.fast and budget.deep can set wall_time, tokens, verify_tokens and agents_max. verify_tokens is per voter; tokens is the review ceiling. For example extend rio/base and set `budget: {fast: {wall_time: 5m, tokens: 100000, verify_tokens: 20000}}`, then validate. Preserve intended steps when overriding lists.
QA's built-in fast budget is 4m/500000 review tokens/60000 per voter; deep 10m/1000000/120000. QA screenshots consume vision tokens. The budget clock continues during local queue pause. Raising a limit is a policy decision, not a fix for missing prerequisites.

sections.title: accounting
sections.body: Reports distinguish requested/configured limits, measured provider usage, cache read/write tokens, estimated prices, and unavailable costs. Do not infer zero cost from absent pricing. Exhausted budgets produce explicit partial/skipped/cancelled work; inspect outcomes and report status. Review result caching can avoid repeated hypotheses, but verification still runs. Council adds bounded members, rounds and experiments; it is opt-in.

sections.title: option-fields
sections.body:
rio/verify@0.1.0:
run: boolean; default=true

topics.title: GitHub and PR reviews
topics.prerequisites: Requires paired endpoint, registered GitHub App installed on the origin repository, and repository review policy. Publication writes GitHub comments/checks. PR policy comes from the merge base, not untrusted head changes. Fork execution requires a self-hosted runner.

sections.title: setup
sections.body:
`rio init --github-app` registers the App through GitHub's manifest flow; --github-org ORG chooses organization ownership. Install the App on intended repositories. `rio doctor` reports installation/endpoint readiness. App permissions include contents read (temporary write only for one thread resolve/unresolve GraphQL mutation), pull_requests write, checks write, metadata read, and organization members read where needed.
Commit .rio/profiles/default.yaml with models and desired `publish: never|ask|auto` to the base branch. rio/base publishes nothing. Open/push events trigger hosted review; maintainers can comment `/rio review` to request/reset review.

sections.title: run
sections.body: `rio review --pr 123` submits/polls the endpoint review and opens findings in an eligible terminal. `--format json` is suitable for agents. With publish ask, `--publish` or explicit interactive confirmation authorizes publication. Auto publishes eligible findings and summary; the `never` policy posts no comments or checks. Forks require maintainer escalation before publication. PR check conclusions are neutral; use policy-aware CLI exit codes for CI gating.

sections.title: recovery
sections.body:
Inspect report.publication for counts/URLs/reason. Exit 5 means publication failed after an otherwise passing review; do not rerun blindly without checking existing comments. Later rounds edit existing comments by identity rather than duplicating them. `/rio dismiss ID REASON [note]` accepts authorized collaborators and 8-character-or-longer unambiguous IDs.
`rio doctor --rotate` rotates webhook secret; `rio init --replace-private-key FILE.pem` updates App private key. Verify the new key before deleting the old one in GitHub. Missing installation: follow the diagnostic install URL; unknown endpoint protocol: update paired versions.

topics.title: Rounds and finding history
topics.prerequisites: Requires online endpoint/API token and a repository identity. Feedback changes endpoint finding state; it does not alter review policy or suppressions. Lineage needs a checked-out branch.

sections.title: rounds
sections.body: `rio review --since-last` continues a branch lineage; `--reset-lineage` starts a new generation and requires --since-last. Repository key normalizes origin URL or falls back to directory name. Branch rebases preserve lineage. Endpoint owns rounds; losing the local cache does not reset them. Beyond rounds.cap, unresolved issues are summarized as reconsideration; report/fail_on still consider findings.

sections.title: answer
sections.body:
`rio feedback 8c1e4a9b --dismiss intentional --note "documented behavior"`. Reasons: fixed, wrong, intentional, irrelevant, style. Use an actual ID with at least 8 characters, unique among findings. Actor uses git user.email when set. Exit 0 recorded; 2 invalid reason/ID or missing endpoint/token; 3 rejected, missing, or ambiguous finding. Ambiguity lists matching identities.
Intentional/irrelevant/style are remembered while the enclosing symbol is unchanged. Wrong is not remembered; recurrence cites the earlier answer. Fixed findings that return are regressions. `rio review --show-remembered` lists remembered entries without changing exit policy.

sections.title: history
sections.body: `rio findings --status dismissed --format json`; optional --rule RULE and --since RFC3339 timestamp. Status values open|fixed|dismissed. No endpoint exits 2. TUI F opens history. Repeated style/irrelevant dismissals can propose a suppression; nothing is suppressed until applied. Fix code for real defects; do not use a dismissal to claim a failed check ran successfully.

topics.title: Suppression proposals
topics.prerequisites: Requires endpoint/API token and repository. Apply writes .rio/profiles/default.yaml and marks the endpoint proposal applied; decline changes proposal state. Review evidence before mutation.

sections.title: list
sections.body: `rio suppressions list --format json` shows proposals and evidence; --status proposed|applied|declined filters. Repeated irrelevant/style dismissals (default three in 90 days) can propose rule/directory suppressions. No automatic suppression follows from a proposal. The report footer and TUI S expose them too.

sections.title: apply
sections.body: `rio suppressions apply PROPOSAL_ID` shows proposed YAML and asks confirmation. Only y applies; anything else keeps profile and proposal unchanged and exits 1. --yes intentionally bypasses the prompt for automation. The default profile is created extending rio/base when absent. Rio writes and validates a temporary sibling before atomic replacement; validation/write failure preserves original bytes. Commit the resulting profile change.

sections.title: decline
sections.body: `rio suppressions decline PROPOSAL_ID --note "still useful"` records rejection and avoids proposing the entry for 180 days. Do not substitute a finding ID for a proposal ID. General failures: 2 usage/config/validation; 3 endpoint/repository/persistence. If profile application succeeds but endpoint update fails, inspect the profile and proposal before retrying; never assume a remote error means no local effect.

topics.title: Security review
topics.prerequisites: Security agent execution requires hosted AI configuration. Secrets scanning also runs locally. Security profiles may enable council; vendors and credentials need separate opt-in. Source/evidence can reach configured providers.

sections.title: run
sections.body: `rio review --profile rio/security` selects the security profile; inspect it first with `rio profile show rio/security`. The rio/security step uses catalog owasp-top10-2025 or asvs-5.0. rio/security built-in uses thorough posture and ASVS; rio/base includes the step disabled. Copy all desired steps if customizing the list.

sections.title: findings
sections.body: Reports show assessed, unassessed and not-applicable catalog items, with security findings and evidence. Trace roles identify source, intermediary steps and sink; a missing guard is distinct from proof of exploitation. Review severity and evidence_level separately. A plausible issue is not a reproduced exploit, and a catalog review is not a certification.

sections.title: policy
sections.body: The rio/security step’s with.fail_on sets evidence, categories, states and rules; its default fails new/worsened security findings at plausible or stronger. validate against the installed schema/profile. Default general fail_on categories do not automatically make every security hypothesis fail. Budget/time/model failures remain visible as incomplete work. Inspect the profile's security policy before using results as a CI gate. Pending live evaluation gates remain pending even when the code is implemented.

sections.title: option-fields
sections.body:
rio/security@0.2.0:
enabled: boolean; default=false
posture: enum; enum=["critical-only","balanced","thorough"]; default="thorough"
max_defects: integer; minimum=1
catalog: enum; enum=["owasp-top10-2025","asvs-5.0"]; default="owasp-top10-2025"
fail_on: object; default={"evidence":"plausible","categories":["security"],"states":["new","worsened"],"rules":[],"incomplete":true,"required_checks":[]}; extra=false
fail_on.evidence: enum; enum=["reproduced","static_proven","plausible","refuted"]
fail_on.categories: array; uniqueItems=true
fail_on.categories[]: enum=["defect","risk","security"]
fail_on.states: array; uniqueItems=true
fail_on.states[]: enum=["new","worsened","pre-existing","fixed","unclassified"]
fail_on.rules: array
fail_on.rules[]: string
fail_on.incomplete: boolean
fail_on.required_checks: array; uniqueItems=true
fail_on.required_checks[]: enum=["typecheck","lint","secrets","coverage","dependencies"]

topics.title: Independent council
topics.prerequisites: Council is hosted, opt-in, and sends finding evidence to allowlisted vendors. Implementation exists; the change's final/live A/B acceptance tasks remain pending. It does not turn agreement into proof.

sections.title: configure
sections.body: rio/base keeps council disabled; rio/security and rio/critical enable it with placeholder members until configured. `rio init` offers council setup; --no-council skips it. --council-vendor accepts the deployment's vendor:family:model entry syntax (see command help). Profile council.vendors_allowed and deployment COUNCIL_VENDORS must both allow a vendor before a pack is built/sent. Self-hosted members require runner model capability.

sections.title: behavior
sections.body: Triggers include plausible high-severity findings, verifier disagreement, high risk, deep and nightly runs. Members independently assess identical evidence, may request bounded experiments, and exchange one structured round. Default limits: two experiments, two rounds, minimum three members. A base-pass/head-fail experiment can reproduce; demonstrated protection can refute; remaining issues stay plausible with a human-readable note. Agreement count/learned weights cannot promote evidence tiers.

sections.title: inspect
sections.body: Inspect per-finding council decision/tier, members/roles, experiments, note and partial markers plus cost. Missing/excluded/timed-out members must be visible. Audit records track vendors, model routes and pack hashes; do not log pack contents. Exceeding a budget cannot justify silently calling the council complete. Use profiles/budgets to tune it; consult live acceptance records before relying on quality claims.

sections.title: option-fields
sections.body:
rio/council@0.1.0:
enabled: boolean; default=false

topics.title: Browser QA
topics.summary: Set up and run browser journeys
topics.prerequisites: Requires Git repository, Linux Docker host with firewall control, paired QA image, app launch contract, synthetic fixtures/seed, journeys, and Codex subscription or host keychain model route (codex/pi harness). QA executes the app/browser in isolated containers and stores evidence; init writes contracts/proposals/journeys. Local judgments are unverified without an endpoint.

sections.title: setup
sections.body:
From Rio source build `docker build -f worker/Dockerfile.qa -t rio-qa:0.1.0 .`. In the application repository define .rio/qa.yaml, seed/fixture definitions and REVIEW.md guidance. tests/fixtures/qa-sample is the complete reference app. Prefer http://app.test:PORT for container HTTP; bare app may trigger Chromium HSTS.
`rio qa validate`; `rio qa seed build`; `rio qa init`; `rio qa list`; `rio qa --full`. Init can propose missing setup and write .rio/qa.proposed.yaml; review it before `rio qa init --accept-contract`. --force replaces validated journeys, not arbitrary existing environment/seed definitions, and protects concurrent edits. Unknown/Compose-only topology can need a reviewed Dockerfile.qa.

sections.title: run
sections.body: `rio qa` selects changed coverage; --full all journeys; --journey NAME repeatable, conflicts with --full. --baseline compares base/head. --cell mobile/dark selects one valid cell. --staged/--base REF select source snapshots. --harness codex|pi chooses driver; --profile requires QA enabled (default rio/qa). --format terminal|json|md|sarif selects output; --no-tui streams, --no-color/--ascii control display. --publish requests publication under the existing transport/policy.

sections.title: inspect
sections.body: `rio qa show` resolved contract; `rio qa show NAME` journey JSON; `rio qa rules` rubric/probes; `rio qa fixtures status` available fixtures. Invalid contracts exit 2 before startup. No endpoint: judged findings/recommendations stay unverified. UX recommendations distinguish observed friction from proposed benefit and cannot fail the review. Check missing-image, authentication, blocked-host and readiness diagnostics before increasing budgets.

sections.title: option-fields
sections.body:

topics.title: Journeys and owner guidance
topics.prerequisites: Journeys live under .rio/qa/journeys and depend on a valid .rio/qa.yaml. Writing/accepting generated proposals changes repository files. Browser authoring requires the isolated QA runtime and model authentication.

sections.title: author
sections.body:
Write REVIEW.md with user goals, recovery, accessibility and intentional design choices. `rio qa init` generates journeys from the seeded application using scoped guidance. Existing journeys get .proposed.yaml candidates; --force permits validated replacement but not concurrent edit loss. `rio qa list` distinguishes runnable and proposed journeys. Validate before committing.
Journey contracts define persona, coverage paths/routes, preconditions, steps, success criteria, viewports and dependency chains. `rio qa show checkout` shows the resolved contract. Use the paired schema and sample app rather than inventing step keys.

sections.title: chains
sections.body: `after` dependencies retain predecessor state; a chain head can use `resets: true`. Combining after with resets is invalid. Dependent viewport sets must be subsets of all prerequisites. Each chain gets restored seed/fresh browser context per viewport/color cell. Members must use the same resolved context.time (or all live); missing time inherits fixture defaults, not predecessor values.

sections.title: sync
sections.body: `rio qa sync --check` is read-only reconciliation: exits 1 when covered source or applicable REVIEW.md changed without journey updates. --staged/--base REF selects comparison. `rio qa sync` re-walks stale journeys and writes validated proposed replacements, preserving committed journeys and concurrent edits. Review proposals, update committed journeys deliberately, validate, then rerun --check. Incomplete authoring writes no proposals.

topics.title: Seeds and fixtures
topics.prerequisites: Requires the isolated Docker app pod, reviewed QA/seed/fixture definitions and app readiness. Seed commands execute only in the app container. Use synthetic accounts/data; credentials come from runtime auth, not committed archives. Build/export do not invoke models.

sections.title: commands
sections.body:
`rio qa seed build` restores a matching snapshot or executes seed steps and captures one. --force rebuilds without changing the fingerprint or deleting leased snapshots. `rio qa seed status [--image APP_IMAGE]` reports fingerprint/cache/rebuild reason; missing image digest is a prerequisite error, never an invented key.
`rio qa seed export NEW_DIRECTORY` verifies archive/part hashes and writes opaque archives plus manifest.json. Parent must exist; destination must be new and not a symlink. It does not unpack archives. `rio qa seed prune --keep 3` retains newest snapshots and active leases; pruning deletes eligible cache data.

sections.title: fixtures
sections.body: `rio qa fixtures status` inspects named uploads, service doubles and captured-message fixtures. Define external service recordings, upload files and capture assertions in the QA fixture contract. app.test maps to the app container. Unmocked hosts/TLS rejection diagnostics explain precondition_failed journeys; fabricated host claims cannot establish dependency failure. Model setup can propose doubles, but unresolved pinned TLS/SDK dependencies require owner action.

sections.title: cache
sections.body: Fingerprint includes manifests, migrations, fixture recordings/uploads, datastore kinds, seed.cache_version and resolved image digest. Shell seed commands conservatively include captured source. Persona credentials are excluded and applied after restore. Change seed.cache_version for external inputs that alter seed semantics. Chains restore seed for isolation. Oversized archives fail with seed_too_large; inspect largest archive instead of leaking production data into fixtures.

topics.title: QA evidence and UX
topics.prerequisites: QA evidence can contain application data; use synthetic fixtures and masks. Hosted evidence operations require endpoint/API token. Prune deletes evidence and revokes download links.

sections.title: inspect
sections.body:
QA captures masked screenshots, DOM and traces per journey/viewport/color scheme and base/head. Open cell detail in TUI to inspect artifacts and guidance citations; image viewing support depends on terminal capability. Local downloaded endpoint screenshots are cached seven days with a 200 MB limit.
Deterministic probes and owner-guided UX judgment are separate. A journey can pass while producing UX recommendations. Reports distinguish observation from suggested benefit and verified from unverified; recommendations cannot fail the review.

sections.title: troubleshoot
sections.body: Validate contracts first, then inspect seed/app readiness, blocked-host diagnostics and browser step artifacts. A dependency failure marks dependent journeys precondition_failed while unrelated journeys continue. A harness/model timeout is incomplete evidence, not proof of no issue. Check report status and per-cell outcomes before exporting.

sections.title: retention
sections.body: `rio qa evidence prune --review REVIEW_ID` deletes hosted evidence for that review and revokes signed downloads. Confirm the report no longer needs those artifacts before running. Review cache retention and raw-output policies separately: deleting a downloaded image does not delete hosted objects, and uninstall does not scan repositories for caches.

topics.title: Continuous integration
topics.prerequisites: CI must install project dependencies/tools before running Rio and choose the intended diff. Hosted mode needs endpoint credentials; local mode works without them. Do not expose credentials to untrusted fork jobs. Review may execute project code.

sections.title: run
sections.body:
Fetch enough Git history for the merge base. `rio doctor --base origin/main --format json`; `rio review --base origin/main --format json > rio-report.json`. For offline local execution add --offline and apply external network isolation if required. CI disables TUI; explicit --format makes output stable.
Save the exit code while uploading artifacts, then exit with it. Exit 0 does not guarantee every optional check ran; enforce fail_on.required_checks for required typecheck/lint. Avoid `|| true` as a final gating policy. Profile comes from the reviewed setup; PR mode applies merge-base policy at the endpoint.

sections.title: sarif
sections.body: `rio review --base origin/main --format sarif > rio.sarif`. Upload with GitHub's code-scanning SARIF action and security-events write permission where supported. Preserve the review exit code even when upload runs after failure. SARIF 2.1.0 contains invocation errors for exits 2/3 and no results for those failures. No output is guaranteed after parser errors or second interrupt; check file existence/validity before upload.

sections.title: limits
sections.body: Shallow clone: fetch deeper history; partial clone: hydrate objects before review. Bare repositories/conflicted selections are refused. Submodules are gitlinks, LFS stays pointers. Hosted checks without vendored/installed dependencies can skip; running hosted review does not install dependencies automatically. PR App check runs are neutral and should not replace explicit fail_on-based gating.

topics.title: Cache, privacy and offline limits
topics.prerequisites: Caches contain source snapshots and evidence and must be protected like the repository. Rio's --offline guarantee applies to Rio requests, not project subprocesses. Use external isolation when all network must be blocked.

sections.title: data
sections.body: Local review uses selected immutable snapshots, extracted source trees, profiles, findings, graph and redacted tool output. Source snapshots can still contain committed secrets. Each tool uses a disposable copy; cached source is not a writable hard-linked tool directory. Dependencies can be linked from worktree installations. Hosted mode uploads base/head snapshots to your endpoint; allowlisted model providers receive bounded context/evidence. OSV auditing sends changed package identities/versions to api.osv.dev.

sections.title: retention
sections.body: Default .rio/cache, age 30d, size 5GiB; override user config cache.dir/max_age/max_size or corresponding RIO_CACHE_* variables. Raw streams are redacted and capped at 16MiB each (head/tail); cache.retain_raw_output=false disables them. Unix directories/files use 0700/0600; Windows inherits ACLs. Run records are per execution; locks/leases protect concurrent runs and pruning.

sections.title: recovery
sections.body: Full disk: inspect doctor effective cache path and free space; lower limits or deliberately remove unneeded repository caches after active runs finish. Missing lineage cache refetches endpoint state; only --reset-lineage resets generation. Uninstall removes binaries, optionally config, but does not find/delete every repository cache. Agent hypothesis cache can replay unchanged context; verification still runs. Set cache:false on rio/agents with to disable it while preserving other desired steps.

topics.title: Evaluation tooling
topics.prerequisites: Requires python3 and Rio's eval/ source directory (current Rio checkout or RIO_EVAL_DIR). The installed binary alone cannot run this developer harness. Evaluation can invoke reviews/models and write datasets/results; use dedicated fixtures/accounts.

sections.title: noise
sections.body: `rio eval noise --help` forwards harness options. Run known-clean PR cases to write noise adjudication skeletons and a summary. Preserve case identifiers, baseline classification, model routes, dates and budgets. Independently adjudicate findings; zero machine-reported issues alone does not establish quality.

sections.title: incidents
sections.body: `rio eval import-incident PR_URL FIX_PR_URL --help` forwards options for turning a PR/fix pair into an incident case. Supply actual URLs and inspect the harness help before a live import. Arguments after the subcommand are forwarded to isolated Python scripts; the harness must exist locally.

sections.title: gates
sections.body: Missing harness exits 2 with setup advice; Python launch failure exits 3; otherwise harness status is propagated. Release evidence and live council A/B gates are separate from passing unit tests. Current repository records do not establish a stable acceptance pass. Consult version-specific evidence rather than promoting implementation status into a quality claim.

topics.title: Read embedded documentation
topics.prerequisites: No repository, configuration, credentials, tools or network required. Documentation is embedded with the binary and read-only; English content is compact for agents. The human Wiki is also available in pt-BR, but retrieval never fetches it.

sections.title: retrieve
sections.body:
`rio docs` or `rio docs list` returns a short index. `rio docs review` returns one topic. `rio docs profiles --section inheritance` returns one section plus required context. Available section and related topic IDs appear in responses. No full-manual dump is offered.
`rio docs search "dependency mismatch"` returns references, not full bodies; --limit 1..10 (default 5). Empty or over-256-byte queries fail; no matches succeeds. Topic/section IDs address embedded content, never filesystem paths/URLs.

sections.title: output
sections.body: All forms accept --format text|json. JSON schema_version 1 includes rio_version, rio_commit, docs_revision, kind and data. No ANSI, pager, TUI or progress. Exit 0 success; 2 usage/unknown topic/section; 3 internal/output failure. Semantic errors after parsing produce JSON kind:error when requested; parser errors go to stderr instead. Text errors go to stderr with empty stdout.

sections.title: budgets
sections.body: Complete text: index/search/section <=4KiB and <=800 reference tokens; topic <=8KiB and <=1800 tokens. JSON <=12KiB and <=3000 tokens. Reference tokenizer: pinned o200k_base; other models count differently. Oversized authored topics fail checks and must be split, never silently clipped. Query only the topics needed for the task. Binary version controls documentation; a newer Wiki does not change it.

topics.title: Steps, rules and adapters
topics.prerequisites: Profile steps form a validated dependency graph. Third-party module loading is not supported. Use the installed built-ins and validate before running project tools or hosted models.

sections.title: pipeline
sections.body:
prepare selects/snapshots/excludes files; checks runs deterministic tools; graph builds bounded impact; triage routes risk; agents propose hypotheses; security applies catalogs; qa exercises browser journeys; verify independently tests hypotheses; council adds opt-in independent evidence assessment; report applies policy and renders. Each step has id, uses, needs, optional parallel/with/rules/agents according to its schema. Lists replace inherited lists.
Default graph bounds: hops 2, max_nodes 2000. rio/checks options include typecheck, lint, secrets, coverage, dependencies, baseline and trust_installed_dependencies. Enable/disable under that step's with; preserve prepare/report and valid dependencies. rio/agents cache:false disables hypothesis reuse.

sections.title: tools
sections.body: TypeScript: tsc, ESLint, Vitest/Jest. Python: Pyright/mypy, Ruff, pytest/coverage.py. Rust: cargo check, configured Clippy/rustfmt, optional cargo llvm-cov. Project-local executables precede PATH. Install project dependencies first. Workspaces schedule affected roots/dependents; checks compare head/base where compatible. Known lockfile/install mismatch cannot be overridden by trust_installed_dependencies.

sections.title: rules
sections.body: Rules and module manifests constrain allowed predicates, effects and options. Use built-in profile examples and the generated Wiki module/schema reference for long inventories; validate every edit with rio profile validate. Typical triggers route high-risk paths, evidence/severity, verifier split, deep/nightly modes; do not assume arbitrary expressions are supported. General fail_on and security policy determine gating, not raw count of agent opinions. For exact installed options, inspect rio profile show and module reference topics.

steps[].file: string; pattern="^(?!/)(?![A-Za-z]:)(?!.*(?:^|/)\\.\\.(?:/|$))(?!.*\\\\).+$"; minLength=1
steps[].applies_to: array *; minItems=1; uniqueItems=true
steps[].applies_to[]: string
users: array *; minItems=0
users[].persona: string *; pattern="^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
users[].apply: string *; minLength=1
paths: array *; minItems=0; uniqueItems=true
paths[]: string

topics.title: Fixture fields 1
topics.prerequisites: Schema reference for qa-fixtures. Edit the corresponding YAML intentionally; validate with rio profile validate or rio qa validate. * means required; extra=false rejects unknown keys. Semantic constraints and prerequisites are in the related guide.

sections.title: fields-1
sections.body:
version: value *; const=1
files: array; minItems=0
files[].name: string *; pattern="^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
files[].path: string; pattern="^\\.rio/qa/fixtures/files/(?!.*(?:^|/)\\.\\.(?:/|$))[^\\\\]+$"
files[].generate: object; extra=false
files[].generate.kind: enum *; enum=["image","pdf","csv","json","text","binary"]
files[].generate.size: integer; minimum=1
files[].generate.width: integer; minimum=1
files[].generate.height: integer; minimum=1
files[].generate.rows: integer; minimum=1

sections.title: fields-2
sections.body:
services: array; minItems=0
services[].name: string *; pattern="^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
services[].kind: enum *; enum=["http-mock","smtp-capture","sms-capture","webhook-sink","oauth-provider","s3","custom"]
services[].env: object *
services[].claims: array; minItems=0; uniqueItems=true
services[].claims[]: string
services[].recordings: string; pattern="^(?!/)(?![A-Za-z]:)(?!.*(?:^|/)\\.\\.(?:/|$))(?!.*\\\\).+$"; minLength=1
services[].behaviors: array; minItems=0; uniqueItems=true
services[].behaviors[]: string
services[].default_behavior: string; pattern="^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"

sections.title: fields-3
sections.body:
services[].start: string; minLength=1
services[].ready: string; minLength=1
capture: object; extra=false
capture.mail: boolean
capture.sms: boolean
capture.webhooks: boolean
defaults: object; extra=false
defaults.time: string; format="date-time"
defaults.timezone: string; minLength=1
defaults.locale: string; minLength=1

sections.title: fields-4
sections.body:
defaults.geolocation: object; extra=false
defaults.geolocation.latitude: number *; minimum=-90; maximum=90
defaults.geolocation.longitude: number *; minimum=-180; maximum=180
defaults.geolocation.accuracy: number; minimum=0
defaults.network: enum; enum=["online","slow-3g","offline"]

topics.title: QA environment fields 2
topics.prerequisites: Schema reference for qa-config. Edit the corresponding YAML intentionally; validate with rio profile validate or rio qa validate. * means required; extra=false rejects unknown keys. Semantic constraints and prerequisites are in the related guide.

sections.title: fields-1
sections.body:
rules.ignore_console: array; minItems=0; uniqueItems=true
rules.ignore_console[]: string
evidence: object; extra=false
evidence.video: boolean
evidence.retention_days: integer; minimum=1
seed: object; extra=false
seed.manifest: string; pattern="^(?!/)(?![A-Za-z]:)(?!.*(?:^|/)\\.\\.(?:/|$))(?!.*\\\\).+$"; minLength=1
seed.migrations: array; minItems=0; uniqueItems=true
seed.migrations[]: string
seed.max_size: value; oneOf=[{"type":"integer","minimum":1},{"type":"string","pattern":"^[1-9][0-9]* ?(B|KiB|MiB|GiB)$"}]

sections.title: fields-2
sections.body:
seed.fallback_rebuild: boolean
seed.cache_version: value; oneOf=[{"type":"string","minLength":1},{"type":"integer","minimum":0}]
